title: Why Do Crypto Transactions Cost Fees? Gas Fees Explained (Beginner Guide)
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Why sending crypto costs a fee, and why the fee changes. Plain English for beginners. AI-generated voice.

scenes.head: WHY THE FEE?
scenes.narration: You send crypto and get charged a fee. Why does that happen, and why does the fee keep changing?

scenes.head: WHO GETS PAID
scenes.narration: Thousands of computers run a blockchain and check every transfer. The fee pays them for that work.

scenes.head: WHY IT CHANGES
scenes.narration: Space in each block is limited. When many people send at once, they compete, and fees rise. When it is quiet, fees fall.

scenes.head: GAS FEES
scenes.narration: On Ethereum the fee is called gas. You pay it in that network's own coin, and every network works differently.

scenes.head: FEES ARE NOT THE PRICE
scenes.narration: Fees are separate from the price of what you send. A tiny transfer can still cost a fee, so small amounts can feel expensive.

scenes.head: BEFORE YOU SEND
scenes.narration: Before you send, check the fee and the network. Sending a small test amount first is a common beginner habit.
